heading: Downstream performance improves predictably with scale or lower pretraining loss
definition: performance on downstream tasks improves predictably with scale or with pretraining loss.
summary: Independent groups have predicted average downstream error and selected task accuracies under specific conditions. The general claim remains contested: individual task forecasts can be inaccurate, and some tasks worsen with scale.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for unrestricted V6 at <1B, 1-10B, 10-100B and >100B; conditional R2 support for selected held-out forecasts at 1-10B and 10-100B. versions.V6.studies_by_size has no separate toy category.
suggested_status.reason: Independent held-out forecasts support conditional predictability: chained laws predict average downstream error at 6.9B (arXiv:2403.08540#R12, arXiv:2403.08540#R13, arXiv:2403.08540#R14), and Model Ladders predicts selected task accuracies at 7B and 13B (arXiv:2412.04403#r19, arXiv:2412.04403#r27). The unrestricted improvement claim is contested: Pythia exhibits inverse parameter/token trends across 70M–12B on preselected tasks (arXiv:2305.14681#HN-p, arXiv:2305.14681#HN-t). Separately, tentative late-training declines on Resisting Correction and Repetitive Algebra at 12B warrant challenges for those conditions (arXiv:2305.14681#RC12B, arXiv:2305.14681#RA12B). TruthfulQA records reversals within sub-billion UnifiedQA models and at GPT-3 175B (arXiv:2109.07958#r17, arXiv:2109.07958#r18, arXiv:2109.07958#r4). Accurate aggregates also coexist with large individual-task forecast errors (arXiv:2403.08540#R19). counts: versions.V6.verdicts records support, limits and challenges; versions.V6.studies_by_size establishes coverage, not replication status within each bin.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent, prospectively specified forecasts across held-out sizes and families, especially above 100B, could establish R2 for a narrower claim with explicit task, metric, loss definition, training recipe, horizon and error tolerance. Aggregate forecasts and individual-run forecasts require separate validation.

wording_issues.issue: Observed ordering, correlation, in-sample fit, interpolation and held-out extrapolation establish different things. Griffin supplies monotonic benchmark averages without a predictive law; PolyPythias describes seed/checkpoint trajectories; the ViT held-out check extrapolates downstream 10-shot error beyond the fitted architecture ranges, without testing orders-of-magnitude extrapolation; the tool-use composition law evaluates held-out FLOP extrapolation. The statement should distinguish these evidential claims.

Forecast quality requires a target, horizon and holdout design. Sigmoid backtests worsen over longer compute horizons; strict largest-model BIG-Bench holdouts perform worse than interpolation; chess run-level and size holdouts differ; accurate TTS identity forecasts coexist with much larger WER errors. Predictability is therefore conditional on what is withheld and forecast.

Improvement is not unconditional or monotonic. TruthfulQA truthfulness declines across GPT-3 family endpoints; ESM2 fitness prediction deteriorates below its favorable perplexity regime; OLMo-1B MATH500 has a downward token trend; enlarging CLIP's text encoder beyond its optimum worsens zero-shot performance while training loss falls. Floors, plateaus, local reversals and inverse trends require stated conditions.

Parameters, tokens, training FLOPs, unique data, adaptation examples, inference budget and component capacity are different predictors. OPT size ordering changes between matched FLOPs and matched tokens; Japanese-specific ability tracks language-specific budget; MoE comparisons require active versus total parameter accounting; tool-use prediction improves when composition accompanies quantity. The scaling variable and held-fixed conditions need specification.

The evidence uses distinct quantities. Densing law uses conditional downstream answer loss; COD's matched-loss comparisons use training loss; the retrieval study uses fine-tuning evaluation loss; the vision-transfer study predicts from upstream classification accuracy. These should retain their measurement names rather than stand interchangeably for held-out pretraining loss. The intended direction should also be explicit: improvement generally accompanies decreasing loss.

A loss-to-score mapping needs its corpus, tokenizer, normalization, architecture, training phase and adaptation conditions. Vocabulary changes can reverse raw-loss ordering; ELMo curricula break simple perplexity-to-GLUE ordering; optimizer changes produce different accuracy at matched loss; SMELT exceeds scores predicted by a Baseline-architecture loss calibration. Lower scalar loss is not sufficient across these interventions.

Predictable aggregate performance does not establish predictable improvement on every task, instance or metric. Chained-loss benchmark averages coexist with large individual HellaSwag errors; Signal and Noise predicts its aggregate more successfully than its math primary score, but averaging training checkpoints substantially improves the math aggregate prediction while individual-task failures persist; Gemstones predicts average error more successfully than task accuracy. The math checkpoint comparison is mixed evidence rather than an absent predictive effect.

The evaluation procedure can change the apparent size trend. DeepSeek-V3.2 humor judging shows size-ordered win rates for Qwen3 models; aggregate human rankings show no significant model effect, and low-agreement themes show no model effect or size-ordered mean ranks. Negated prompts induce inverse trends; output-token constraints can favor smaller reasoning models; trace-length correction reverses several model rankings. The outcome, prompt, judge, decoding and inference budget belong in the claim's conditions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Scale variable, matched budget and capacity allocation
method_sensitivity.what: OPT size ordering reverses between matched FLOPs and matched tokens or steps. Cerebras-GPT's regular parameter trend uses approximately constant tokens per parameter, while fixed-token comparator frontiers bend; this curve-shape difference does not itself establish failed downstream prediction. Within the CC12M CLIP architecture grid, total-parameter LOOCV R² is 0.240, versus 0.937 when separate encoder sizes and a capacity-mismatch penalty are included. This is within-grid cross-validation. NeuroJEPA configurations at similar compute give different downstream errors. Parameters, unique data, consumed tokens, compute and component allocation therefore require separate specification.

method_sensitivity.factor: Loss definition, normalization and validation construction
method_sensitivity.what: Across vocabulary sizes, raw language-model loss reverses its association with downstream accuracy: higher raw loss accompanies better downstream performance. Unigram normalization restores the expected direction. CSV's learned capability-weighted loss improves prediction relative to raw average loss. Causal-LM versus span-corruption perplexity changes post-SFT pairwise ranking prediction from below to above chance. Task-answer NLL, training loss, fine-tuning loss, benchmark BPB and general held-out pretraining loss remain different predictors.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training-data relevance, mixture, diversity and repetition
method_sensitivity.what: HyperCLOVA's within-run perplexity association does not preserve cross-corpus few-shot ranking. Its 1.3B Cafe, KiN and Modu models use corpora of 82.5B, 27.0B and 5.9B tokens respectively, with about 150B tokens of training exposure over 72K steps. Modu has higher perplexity but higher YNAT F1 than Cafe and KiN; the Majority YNAT F1 baseline is 8.26. Matched-data loss-to-loss curves shift more under data interventions than under the tested non-data changes. Accurate conventional compute extrapolation fails under repetition, while repetition-aware InfoLaw improves it. In tool-use SFT, adding composition terms changes held-out normalized-score MAE from 0.1706 for task count alone to 0.0285. Unique data, repeated exposure and task relevance are distinct changes.

Looped Transformers outperform non-looped models at matched validation loss on reasoning-heavy groups. MoE expert-count changes can lower pretraining loss while worsening math/code outcomes. Baseline-calibrated loss-to-score mappings underpredict SMELT across scales. GPTQ 3/4-bit configurations support fitted size relationships. Under 2-bit quantization, models below 2B collapse toward random performance with adjusted R²<0; reasoning tasks at N≥4B show complete failure with a flat surface and adjusted R²≈0.22. These specified 2-bit conditions show absent scaling effects. A shared scalar loss does not remove architecture, objective or precision effects.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation metric, task format, judge and benchmark inclusion
method_sensitivity.what: Arithmetic appears smoother under token edit distance or greater measurement resolution. MMLU loss–compute R² changes from 0.28 for letter-scored MCQ to 0.68 for continuation and 0.61 for modified MCQ. Signal and Noise predictions change with primary score versus BPB and checkpoint averaging. For its math aggregate, primary-score absolute prediction error is 11.33% with final checkpoints only and 2.30% with averaged training checkpoints; corresponding relative errors are 65.52% and 13.28%. Individual-task failures persist. Qwen3 humor has an automated size trend, while aggregate human rankings show no significant model effect. Metric smoothing, aggregate averaging and benchmark selection each change what predictability is being assessed.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prompting, demonstrations, context and inference budget
method_sensitivity.what: NeQA GPT-3 accuracy declines with size under zero-shot evaluation but rises under few-shot chain-of-thought. Across PaLM 8B, 62B and 540B, standard-prompt AQuA accuracy is 19.3%, 25.6%, 25.2%, whereas StrategyQA rises monotonically at 55.6%, 58.4%, 68.6%. Under the specified 150-output-token GSM8K setting, Qwen2.5-7B scores 48.1 versus 39.0 for 14B. Scene-editing trends differ between operation selection, selector resolution and host-resolved argument extraction. Scaffolded operation selection gives both Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct 7B and 14B 95%, an absent gain in that comparison; this descriptive plateau does not establish failure of a fitted forecasting law. Prompt, context access and execution budget can alter both curve shape and size ordering.

method_sensitivity.factor: Adaptation stage, optimizer, schedule and checkpoint selection
method_sensitivity.what: For base models excluding Gemma, pre-fine-tuning perplexity rankings versus post-task-fine-tuning downstream rankings have mean Kendall τ=0.78. Post-fine-tuning perplexity and instruction-tuned-model perplexity do not directly test V6's pretraining-loss predictor. At fixed 1B and 8B sizes, learning-rate schedules can produce higher validation loss but better post-SFT averages than minimum-loss schedules, reversing the expected ordering. Nexus and AdamW have equal reported mean pretraining loss at 1B but different downstream accuracy. The customer-task study retains a base-model family qualification across Qwen3 0.6B–32B and Llama 1B–8B; its fixed-size post-SFT task-NLL correlations and epoch-axis loss–quality divergence do not test V6.

method_sensitivity.factor: Functional form, fitting range and supplied calibration information
method_sensitivity.what: DataDecide's two-step fits support held-out downstream prediction, single-step fits have substantially worse errors, and the five-parameter two-step fit fails useful numerical prediction. These prediction-error comparisons do not establish V7 exponent or allocation dependence. Removing the 1.4B fitting point raises the reported RedPajama 17-task average relative prediction error from 0.05% to 10.64%. For brackets, preferred VAM and FAM produce different scaling-exponent conclusions. Within the CC12M CLIP architecture grid, prediction improves when encoder-specific sizes and mismatch replace total parameters. Fit quality therefore depends on form, fitting-point selection and whether the predictor represents consequential configuration differences.

method_sensitivity.factor: Holdout design, extrapolation distance and family information
method_sensitivity.what: BIG-Bench prediction is stronger under interpolation than strict largest-model holdouts. Sigmoid backtest errors grow with forecast distance and depend on starting scale. On leaderboard v1, FLOPs prediction has average MAE 7.8 percentage points with shared intercepts and 4.4 with family-specific intercepts; family-specific-intercept Sloth d=3 has 4.2. Test-family calibration uses its smallest model. Chess run-level LOO reward RMSE is 0.0194 versus 0.0242 when withholding model size. Random checkpoint holdouts, new sizes, new families and future populations test different forms of generalization.

method_sensitivity.factor: Seed distribution, aggregation and downstream endpoint
method_sensitivity.what: Synthetic-task means can improve smoothly while seed distributions remain bimodal and individual runs change abruptly. PolyPythias reports declining performance from 10^4 to 10^5 training steps at 14M–160M, and random-level performance on ARC (Challenge), Logiqa, WSC and WinoGrande across 14M–410M. Elementary Pythia capability emergence varies across initialization seeds; mixed copying/repetition success is established collectively at smaller scales, without individual-size attribution.
